summary: Payments broke because the shared ledger-db ran out of disk space (reached 100% at ~14:50–15:00), causing all writes — payment ledger writes, order inserts, WAL appends — to fail with "No space left on device". The disk was already ~89.5% full at 13:00 and climbed steadily BEFORE the payment-service v6.0.0 deploy at 14:46, driven by an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining tens of GB of WAL (up to 92.6 GB). The v6.0.0 mandate flow is a coincidental bystander: rolling it back at 15:12 did NOT recover the service, and errors continued at ~320/period through 16:57. Root cause is resource_exhaustion at ledger-db, matching historical incident HIST-114.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db filled its filesystem because an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retained tens of GB of WAL; when the volume hit 100% (~14:50), all Postgres writes failed with 'No space left on device', breaking payment-service (ledger writes), order-service (order inserts) and any other writer. The fault originates in ledger-db, not payment-service.

causal_chain.claim: Inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retains WAL continuously (33–92 GB) starting before 12:19
Retained WAL drives ledger-db disk usage from 89.5% (13:00) to 100% (~14:50)
At 100% disk, ledger-db write/PANIC errors 'No space left on device' begin 15:01
payment-service ledger writes fail -> error_rate 61%, success 35%
order-service on the same shared DB also fails on INSERTs
Rollback of v6.0.0 does not restore service because the disk is still full

assumptions: Replication slot 'analytics_cdc' belongs to an inactive analytics/CDC consumer that never caught up.
No other large writer contributed comparably.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow overloaded ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 release's new mandate flow (MANDATE_HOLD ledger entries) wrote abnormally and filled the ledger-db, breaking payments.

causal_chain.claim: v6.0.0 deployed 14:46 with new ledger entry type

assumptions: New entry type writes significantly more data than before.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Disk was already 89.5% at 13:00 and 95% at 14:15, well before the 14:46 deploy; the rollback at 15:12 did not recover service and errors continued at 320/period through 16:57; a different service (order-service) sharing ledger-db failed identically at the same time; and the known mechanism is WAL retained by an inactive replication slot.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank-partner-api dependency failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank partner API degraded and caused payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: bank_api_error_rate stayed flat at 0.2% throughout, and the actual errors are ledger DB disk failures, not bank-API errors.

facts.statement: payment-service v6.0.0 (new UPI mandate flow, MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type) deployed 14:46 and rolled back 15:12.
ledger-db disk usage was 89.5% at 13:00 and 100% by ~14:50, before payment errors began.
ledger-db logs repeatedly show inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining up to 92599 MB of WAL and disk-usage warnings up to 98%.
ledger-db raised PANIC 'No space left on device' write errors from 15:01:01.
payment-service logged 179 'ledger write failed ... No space left on device' errors starting 15:00:26.
The 15:12 rollback did not restore service: 320 more errors through 16:57:54.
payment-service error_rate rose to ~61% and payment_success_rate fell to ~35%.
order-service, sharing ledger-db, failed with 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' starting 15:00:42.
bank_api_error_rate stayed flat at 0.2%, ruling out the bank partner API.
ledger-db replication lag rose from ~926 ms (11:00) to ~5221 ms (16:42).
Historical incident HIST-114 was ledger-db disk full from retained WAL due to an inactive replication slot.

assumptions: The replication slot 'analytics_cdc' belongs to an inactive CDC/analytics consumer and its WAL is unused and safe to drop, subject to operator confirmation.
No other single source of write volume (e.g., a bulk backfill) contributed comparably to disk growth; WAL retention is the dominant driver per log evidence.

timeline.event: ledger-db disk ~89% trajectory begins; replication lag ~926 ms and rising
Inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining 63157 MB of WAL
payment-service first 'ledger write failed: No space left on device'
order-service first 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device'
ledger-db PANIC on pg_wal write, no space left
payment-service v6.0.0 rolled back — service does NOT recover

recommended_actions.action: Free space on ledger-db immediately: drop or advance the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (after confirming no consumer needs it) and/or expand the volume; then verify writes resume.
recommended_actions.rationale: The inactive slot's retained WAL is what filled the disk; freeing it is the actual fix since rollback did not help.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating this as a payment-service regression: keep services up, do not re-deploy, and monitor ledger-db disk_used_pct and write success for recovery.
recommended_actions.rationale: The fault is in the shared DB, and the v6.0.0 rollback neither caused nor fixed the outage.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on replication-slot lag/retention and on ledger-db disk_used_pct thresholds (e.g. >85%) with automated WAL-retention alerts.
recommended_actions.rationale: Disk climbed from 80% to 100% over ~3.5h with only WARNs; earlier alerting would have prevented the outage. HIST-114 already recommended a slot-lag alert.

recommended_actions.action: Add disk-capacity headroom/monitoring for the shared ledger-db and audit all replication slots/data-volume consumers; add periodic slot cleanup.
recommended_actions.rationale: A shared datastore serving order/payment/settlement/portfolio services is a single point of failure when its disk fills.

data_gaps: No direct metric for replication slot retention size; WAL retention inferred from log messages only.
No log/telemetry evidence identifying which consumer owns slot 'analytics_cdc' or why it stopped consuming.
ledger-db logs were truncated (returned 20 of 298 matched in one window), so the full sequence of disk warnings is only partially captured.
No evidence yet that disk space was reclaimed between 15:12 and 16:59 (errors persist, implying it was not); a post-remediation confirmation is needed.

findings.statement: payment-service v6.0.0 (new UPI mandate flow, new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD) deployed at 14:46 by p.nair and was rolled back at 15:12.
ledger-db disk usage was already ~89.5% at 13:00 and rose monotonically to 100% by ~14:50, before any payment-service errors began (first error 15:00:26).
ledger-db logs show an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining tens of GB of WAL (up to 92599 MB) repeatedly, and disk-usage warnings escalating 80%→90%→95%→98%.

refs.quote: replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 92599 MB of WAL

findings.statement: ledger-db emits PANIC/write errors 'No space left on device' for pg_wal and base files beginning 15:01:01, continuation of the disk-full condition.

refs.quote: PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478": No space left on device
could not extend file "base/16402/2619": No space left on device

findings.statement: payment-service produced 179 'ledger write failed: ... No space left on device' errors in the 15:00–16:00 window, starting 15:00:26.

refs.quote: ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device

findings.statement: After the 15:12 rollback, payment-service continued erroring: 320 more 'No space left on device' errors from 15:12:08 through 16:57:54.
payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.22% before 14:54 to avg 61% at 15:03 and stayed ~62% through 16:51; payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~35% at 15:00 and stayed there.
order-service (a different, trading-owned service) also fails on the same shared ledger-db with 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' starting 15:00:42 — 236 occurrences.

refs.quote: INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device

findings.statement: ledger-db is a shared postgres datastore used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate stayed flat at 0.2% throughout (13:00–16:45), so the external bank-partner-api was healthy and did not cause the failures.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms climbed steadily from ~926 ms at 11:00 to ~5213 ms at 16:42, consistent with an inactive consumer slot retaining WAL.
No config or feature-flag changes were recorded in the incident window.
Historical incident HIST-114 matches: 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', category resource_exhaustion.

refs.quote: Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled

findings.statement: The disk was already ~95% full at 14:15 and ~96.8% at 14:20, i.e. the exhaustion trajectory predated the 14:46 deploy.
